note: Curated requirement register. The register began as pure recovery: docs/specs/srs.md defined no identifiers, so every statement was recovered from the code, tests, workflows and roadmap rows that cite the identifier. Since 2026-08-26 it carries a second regime under ADR 0007: statements authored forward as product decisions, each marked as authored in its reconstruction note and carrying review "confirmed". Recovered statements keep review "needs-review", because none has been confirmed against an authored specification that survives. Identifiers are adopted verbatim and are never renumbered, because renumbering would invalidate live citations across source and continuous integration.

provenance_vocabulary.reconstructed: A statement recovered from at least one citation that names this identifier and describes a single behavior; or, where the reconstruction note says so, a statement authored as a product decision under ADR 0007.
provenance_vocabulary.unrecoverable: The identifier is asserted by a grouped or ranged citation, but no individual statement can be attributed without inventing the split. No statement is recorded.

implementation_status_vocabulary.implemented: Enforced by shipped code in this repository.
implementation_status_vocabulary.partial: Partly enforced, with a stated remainder.
implementation_status_vocabulary.unknown: No evidence either way in this repository.

alias_note: docs/ROADMAP.md historically wrote three families without the FR- prefix. VIS and EXP are normalized to FR-VIS and FR-EXP because both families use the prefixed form in source. IMP has no prefixed form anywhere, so FR-IMP is this register inferring the family prefix from its two siblings; the inference is recorded here rather than silently applied. The roadmap was rewritten in canonical spellings on 2026-08-26; the aliases stay registered because earlier revisions and commit messages still use the bare forms.

INT.title: Interface and integration requirements
INT.numbering: One to three digits, without zero padding, unlike the FR and NFR families.
INT.note: Declared explicitly so the citation reader recognizes it. The reader will not accept an open LETTERS-digits pattern, because the repository is full of tokens shaped like one: SHA-256, RFC-822, ISO-8601.

unmodelled_markers.observation: T1 is cited beside SRS INT-1 and FR-SET-001 in the authentication middleware; T5 beside SRS INT-5 in the storage adapter. Two members of one shape, each attached to a different subsystem boundary, which suggests a threat or trust-boundary numbering. Two citations still cannot establish what the family asserts, and a single letter followed by a digit cannot be harvested without matching unrelated text throughout the repository. As of 2026-08-26 the two boundaries the markers sit on are modelled by NFR-SEC-001 and NFR-SEC-002, cited on the same source lines; the T markers themselves stay unmodelled and are kept for archaeology.

The original set was organized by quality attribute rather than numbered in one sequence, and almost all of it was lost. The non-functional set that exists today was authored forward under ADR 0007 on 2026-08-26; these two numbers stay unallocated because reusing them for new statements would counterfeit recovery.

INT-3 and INT-5 were invisible until the family was declared to the citation reader, which is why the declaration is recorded in this register rather than hard-coded in the generator.

requirements.title: Full-fidelity export and restore
requirements.statement: Export must write every collection with its document identity and subcollections intact, so that a restore round-trips the graph without loss. Restore must validate bundle integrity before performing any force-replacement write, and a force restore must prune only what the bundle omits.

requirements.title: Related records commit in one transaction
requirements.statement: A capture, interaction, merge, or import commit that produces several records must write the nodes, edges, revisions, and reminders in a single database transaction. Identifiers are pre-allocated so related records can reference each other inside that commit, and every durable mutation records audit history.

requirements.title: Merge undo refuses a record edited since the merge
requirements.statement: Undoing a merge must refuse when any affected record has been edited since the merge was performed, and must report a conflict requiring manual recovery rather than silently destroying the later edit.

requirements.title: Third-party credentials live in a secret store
requirements.statement: Credentials for third-party services must be read from a secret store or an injected environment variable, never persisted in application data. Postgres keeps only non-secret synchronization settings, and a surface that reports credential presence must report presence, not the value.

requirements.title: Health counts come from aggregate queries
requirements.statement: The status page is polled about once a minute, so its node and edge counts must come from aggregate queries rather than from loading the tables.

requirements.title: The thirty-day trash promise is enforced by a purge
requirements.statement: A soft-deleted record must be permanently removed once it ages past the retention window, by a scheduled purge with previewable and dry-runnable commands. Rolling back or discarding a staged import is a deletion intent: the raw upload and the parsed rows must be removed, not retained.

requirements.title: Continuous integration fails loudly rather than skipping
requirements.statement: Every continuous-integration job must fail rather than skip when its preconditions are missing, and must upload the report and traces needed to diagnose a failure.

requirements.title: Duplicate candidates require shared evidence
requirements.statement: A pair may be offered as a duplicate candidate only when the two records share identity, contact, URL or domain, or geography evidence. Opening a screen must not start a full duplicate scan as a side effect.

requirements.title: Export policy checks re-read their referents
requirements.statement: An export policy decision about a referenced record must re-read that record rather than rely on a value retained from an earlier pass.

requirements.title: Oversized and malformed bodies map to 413 and 400
requirements.statement: The request body limit must accommodate a legitimate export or contacts payload of several megabytes, and an oversized or malformed body must produce 413 or 400 carrying a request identifier, never a generic 500. The limit must be applied early enough that a router-local parser cannot bypass it.

requirements.title: Final is an invariant, not a label
requirements.statement: A resume may be marked as sent only when it has been compiled and finalized. A draft must be refused.

requirements.title: Sensitive records are excluded transitively
requirements.statement: A default export must exclude records marked sensitive and everything that depends on them, not only the sensitive records themselves.

requirements.title: Edge endpoint types are enforced on create
requirements.statement: Edge creation must reject a missing endpoint, and must reject an endpoint whose node type is not permitted for that edge type. The permitted matrix is enforced by the API, not only described by form descriptors.

requirements.title: Downloads use the authenticated transport
requirements.statement: A file download must go through the shared API client so that it carries the bearer token and the active data space, rather than issuing a bare fetch.

requirements.title: Development sign-in is loopback-only
requirements.statement: Development sign-in hands any caller a valid owner token, so it must be restricted to loopback requests and must be disabled outside development. The restriction is defence in depth, not the only control.

requirements.title: Workflow actions are pinned to commit SHAs
requirements.statement: Continuous-integration actions must be pinned to commit SHAs rather than to moving tags, so that a compromised or retagged action cannot change what runs.

requirements.title: Search invalidation is a generation counter
requirements.statement: Search index invalidation must be a monotonic generation counter rather than a boolean flag, so that a mutation arriving during a rebuild is not lost.

requirements.title: Selection feasibility includes entry overhead
requirements.statement: Resume selection must budget each candidate at its bullet lines plus its entry overhead, and must report the same cost that the greedy loop budgets with.

requirements.title: Shared shapes are defined once in the core package
requirements.statement: A shape used by both the API and the web application must be defined once in the shared core package rather than redefined route-locally.

requirements.title: Unassigned import lines stay retryable
requirements.statement: An import line that was not assigned to a target creates nothing and must remain retryable with a stated reason. Only a clean run closes a batch, and the raw upload is purged once the batch closes.

requirements.title: Spreadsheet formulas are neutralized in CSV output
requirements.statement: A value written to CSV that a spreadsheet would interpret as a formula must be neutralized before it is written.

requirements.title: Overlays are real dialogs
requirements.statement: An overlay must be a real dialog with an accessible name, a focus trap, dismissal on Escape, and focus restoration, rather than a hand-rolled backdrop element.

requirements.title: Controls carry programmatic labels
requirements.statement: Every visual label must be associated with its control, and a row that behaves as a control must be a real button, so that it is reachable by keyboard and announced as actionable.

requirements.title: Calendar dates are answered in the user timezone
requirements.statement: Any question about today, overdue, due, a streak, or a snooze target must be answered in the user timezone, which the client sends and the server carries for the life of the request.

requirements.title: Liveness, readiness, shutdown, and outbound deadlines
requirements.statement: Liveness and readiness must be separate probes, shutdown must stop accepting traffic before letting in-flight requests finish, outbound HTTP must carry a deadline so a stalled connection cannot hold a request open, and every request must be correlated in the access log.

requirements.title: No published fallback signing key
requirements.statement: The build service signing key is the authentication, so there must be no published fallback value. A published fallback would let any caller sign a request.

requirements.title: Read the graph once per request
requirements.statement: When more than one helper in a request needs the whole graph, the request must load it once and thread it, rather than loading it once per helper.

requirements.title: Per-type counts use one grouped query
requirements.statement: Live node counts per type must come from a single grouped query.

requirements.title: Export holds a per-workspace lock
requirements.statement: Export must take a per-workspace lock so that one workspace export cannot block another.

requirements.title: Keyboard capture grammar
requirements.statement: A single capture line must parse deterministically into a plan of linked records, be previewable before commit, and commit as undoable writes.

requirements.title: Schema-driven entity forms
requirements.statement: Every node type must be creatable and editable through a form rendered from a shared descriptor, which reports field-level validation errors without throwing and rejects a record missing a required property.

requirements.title: Entry fields offer existing values
requirements.statement: A form field must be able to offer existing values from the graph as debounced, keyboard-navigable suggestions.

requirements.title: Attachments go through a storage adapter
requirements.statement: Attachments must be stored through the storage abstraction, and delivery must use private, short-lived signed URLs.

requirements.reconstruction_note: Asserted only by the grouped citation FR-CAP-001/003/005 in docs/ROADMAP.md, whose row text reads "grammar + live preview + commit + undo-able writes". FR-CAP-001 and FR-CAP-003 are pinned individually elsewhere, leaving two unattributed behaviors ("live preview" and "undo-able writes") for one identifier. The statement cannot be recovered without inventing the split.

requirements.title: Note-append targets the last-viewed record
requirements.statement: Capture in note-append mode must attach the note to the record the operator viewed most recently.

requirements.title: An application is a typed record with a status machine
requirements.statement: An application is a graph record carrying a typed status machine, and the career runway groups applications by live stage (draft, applied, screening, interview, offer), with terminal outcomes presented apart from the live stages rather than mixed into them.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007: the career capability shipped with no requirement naming what it does. Enforced by the application property schema in packages/core/src/schema/node-props.ts and the runway grouping in apps/web/src/routes/career/CareerOverview.tsx; neither cites this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: The application dossier joins its whole context
requirements.statement: An application's dossier must join the posting, the tailoring target, the sent résumé, the company, the referrer, and the interview loop into one surface, and must state in one line which context is missing rather than hiding the gap.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. Enforced by the dossier read projection in packages/core/src/schema/application.ts and apps/web/src/routes/career/ApplicationDossier.tsx; neither cites this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: Applications get first-class write endpoints
requirements.statement: Applications must be creatable and editable through first-class endpoints that validate the status machine and its transitions, not only through the generic record API.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007; delivered 2026-08-27. POST and PATCH /applications and POST /applications/:id/status are the first-class doors, and the generic node patch runs the same guard, because the application form's own save goes through it and a guard the back door skips is not a guard. The machine is forward-permissive: any later stage or any outcome is recordable, since plenty of roles have no recruiter screen and refusing to record applied straight to interview would be refusing something that happened; walking backwards and reopening a closed record are what it refuses, and the refusal names both ends of the move. Correction is a separate act with its own door and its own provenance, so an operator who mis-set a record to rejected is not held there and the history can still tell a move from a fixed mistake. The status control offers exactly the moves the server would accept.

requirements.title: The runway leads with next moves
requirements.statement: The career runway must lead with next moves: the due and overdue next steps across live applications, ranked by date, each linking to the application it belongs to.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. Enforced by the next-moves panel in apps/web/src/routes/career/CareerOverview.tsx, which does not cite this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: A correspondence profile per person
requirements.statement: For any person with logged interactions, a correspondence profile must be computable deterministically: reciprocity ratio, median reply latency in each direction, unanswered inbound count, and the distribution of contact days, with each figure decomposing into the interactions that produced it.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007; delivered the same day. correspondenceProfile in packages/core computes the four figures from operator-stated initiated_by directions; GET /people/:id/correspondence serves them; the person profile's correspondence panel opens each figure into the interactions behind it, under a coverage header that owns up to directionless history instead of guessing it.

requirements.title: A network rollup of correspondence health
requirements.statement: A network-level correspondence rollup must rank dormant-but-once-strong ties for reactivation and name the brokers through whom introductions have historically flowed, computed with the same constants the relationship algorithms ship with, so the rollup and the per-tie views cannot disagree.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007 and shipped the same day: packages/core/src/algorithms/correspondence.ts ranks reactivation by re-reading each tie's history with the tie-strength kernel itself, and /network/correspondence presents the rollup with its factor decomposition. Brokers tally the met_via labels the relationship edges already carry.

requirements.title: Introductions are first-class facts
requirements.statement: An introduction must be recordable as a first-class fact (who introduced whom, when, in what context), feeding broker detection, warm-path evidence, and the favor ledger.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007; delivered the same day. The INTRODUCED edge (the twenty-ninth type) records the connected pair with the broker in via; the person profile's log-an-introduction dialog is the recording surface, optionally crediting the broker's favor ledger; the rollup tallies recorded brokers apart from free-text met-via credits; the warm-path search's existing INTRODUCED branch lights up with real edges.

requirements.title: The relationship edge is the record
requirements.statement: A person-to-person relationship must be editable as a record in its own right, carrying its own properties such as topics. A patch replaces properties wholesale, so the client merges before sending.

requirements.title: One-tap interaction logging
requirements.statement: Logging an interaction must create the interaction node and its relationship edge from a single overlay.

requirements.title: An interaction can spawn a follow-up reminder
requirements.statement: Logging an interaction, or committing a dated capture, must be able to create a follow-up reminder in the same commit.

requirements.title: Reconnect lane ordering
requirements.statement: The dashboard reconnect lane must rank ties by a deterministic spaced-repetition score, presenting the strongest need first.

requirements.reconstruction_note: Asserted only by the range citation FR-CON-001..009 in docs/ROADMAP.md, whose row lists five features across nine identifiers. No individual behavior can be attributed to this identifier from any source in the repository.

requirements.title: Contact ranking decomposes into factor chips
requirements.statement: A who-to-call ranking must decompose exactly into the per-factor contributions the interface displays, so that every rank is explained by name and number rather than by color alone.

requirements.title: Ranking weights come from settings
requirements.statement: The weights that rank contacts must be read from settings rather than fixed in the route.

requirements.title: Warm-introduction paths carry per-hop evidence
requirements.statement: A warm-introduction search must run a deterministic bounded traversal from the operator to a target organization and present each path with its per-hop evidence, scoring a path by the product of its hop strengths so that long weak chains rank below short strong ones.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Recovered by elimination: the identifier appears only inside a grouped citation, and every other identifier in that group is pinned individually elsewhere, leaving exactly one unattributed behavior in the group text. Here the group is FR-CON-006..009 on the network-intelligence row of docs/ROADMAP.md; FR-CON-006, FR-CON-007 and FR-CON-009 are pinned individually, leaving warm-introduction paths with per-hop evidence. The behavior is implemented by packages/core/src/algorithms/graph-paths.ts and apps/api/src/routes/v1/intros.ts.

requirements.title: Tie strength recomputes immediately
requirements.statement: Logging an interaction must recompute and persist the affected tie strength within the same request rather than deferring it to a batch.

requirements.title: The favor ledger is part of the relationship record
requirements.statement: A favor must be recordable on the relationship it belongs to, in either direction (owed to the operator or owed by them), with a settle state and dates. The ledger is visible on the person and editable without leaving them, and a concurrent edit to the relationship is refused rather than silently overwritten.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007: the ledger shipped with no requirement naming it. Enforced by the favor properties on the relationship edge in packages/core/src/schema/edge-props.ts and the favors route in apps/api/src/routes/v1/favors.ts, whose concurrency refusal is the EDGE_CHANGED conflict; neither cites this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: A dossier is compiled evidence with a provenance appendix
requirements.statement: A dossier is a named, single-subject selection of evidence records compiled deterministically into a document whose every claim cites the records behind it, closed by a provenance appendix carrying each claim's source, confidence, and revision trail.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 under ADR 0007; delivered 2026-08-27. A dossier stores claims and, for each claim, the records it rests on; compiling one resolves every citation against the live graph and closes the document with a provenance appendix carrying each record's source, confidence and revision trail. Nothing is copied into the selection, so a dossier cannot keep asserting the old title of something renamed. The appendix keeps three answers apart rather than two: a record in the graph, one withdrawn after being cited, and an id nothing ever carried. A withdrawn record still prints, with its history, which is also why a missing citation does not block the compile while a missing required section does.

requirements.title: Dossier templates address named audiences
requirements.statement: Dossier templates must address named audiences (a promotion review, a petition exhibit list, a clearance or background history), each with its own section grammar and inclusion rules, sharing one selection and compile pipeline underneath.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 under ADR 0007; delivered 2026-08-27. Three audiences over one selection format, each with its own section grammar declared as data rather than code: a promotion review argues, so its claims carry several pieces of evidence; an exhibit list enumerates, so an entry is exactly one record and the numbering means something; a background history is read for gaps, so it admits only records that carry dates. GET /dossiers/audiences publishes the grammar and the editor reads it, because the Career workspace's pipeline ordering once lived in the browser and drifted from the server.

requirements.title: Full-fidelity export bundle
requirements.statement: A one-click export must produce a self-describing bundle of JSONL records and a Markdown vault with a checksummed manifest, streamed entry by entry.

requirements.title: Scheduled off-box backups
requirements.statement: The deployment must take scheduled encrypted backups to storage held outside the application host.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Split inferred from the order of the two behaviors named in the backup row of docs/ROADMAP.md, which cites EXP-012/013 without the FR- prefix. Status is partial rather than planned because scripts/backup-to-s3.sh exists and is wired to the backup:s3 package script, while docs/ROADMAP.md still records scheduled backups as an unshipped production concern. That contradiction is recorded as DOC-D-028.

requirements.title: Periodic restore drill
requirements.statement: The deployment must rehearse a full restore from a backup on a stated schedule, and the drill must be documented as a runnable procedure.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Split inferred from the order of the two behaviors named in the backup row of docs/ROADMAP.md, which cites EXP-012/013 without the FR- prefix. docs/runbooks/restore-drill.md documents the procedure; whether it is rehearsed on a schedule is an operational fact this repository cannot evidence.

requirements.title: Restore revives a record and its hidden edges
requirements.statement: Restoring a record from trash must also revive the edges that were hidden when it was deleted, so that recovery is lossless.

requirements.title: A query round-trips through a URL
requirements.statement: A search query and its filter clauses must round-trip through a URL so that a saved view is shareable and reloadable, and saved views can be named and pinned to the navigation.

requirements.reconstruction_note: Asserted only by the grouped citation FR-ORG-001/002/007 in docs/ROADMAP.md, whose row text reads "Trash + restore + history/revisions". FR-ORG-002 is pinned individually as restore, leaving two unattributed behaviors for two identifiers with no evidence of which is which.

requirements.title: Identity integrity workflow
requirements.statement: Duplicate candidates must be presented as a queue, merged on visible evidence, recorded in history with learned aliases, and undoable.
requirements.reconstruction_note: The only citation is the identity-integrity row of docs/ROADMAP.md:22, so the statement is that row restated as a requirement rather than recovered from code. The behavior is implemented: the candidate queue and merge live in apps/api/src/routes/v1/duplicates.ts, and the scoring in packages/core/src/algorithms/dedup.ts. Neither cites the identifier, which is why the attribution is recorded here instead of being inferred silently.

requirements.title: Off-by-default dual flag and kill switch
requirements.statement: The productivity command API and web surfaces stay off unless both VITAE_PRODUCTIVITY_ENABLED and VITE_PUBLIC_PRODUCTIVITY_ENABLED are the tokens true, 1, or yes. Unset or any other value on either flag is the kill switch: the API answers the same 404 as a missing route, and the web hides nav and commands. Committed environment examples remain false.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-09-11 from ADR 0013 and the Task 10 hardening plan. Enforced by apps/api/src/services/productivity/flag.ts and apps/web/src/lib/productivity-flag.ts.

requirements.title: Workspace-safe route, read, and write gating
requirements.statement: When the flags are on, productivity reads and writes stay inside the active workspace and inherit the existing auth, space, and entitlement gates. /today, /today/planner, and /today/ledger do not move. Bookmarks to the gated routes still resolve behind AuthGate to a short not-available page rather than a distinct disabled code.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-09-11 from ADR 0013. Enforced by apps/api/src/routes/v1/productivity.ts and the web shell nav in apps/web/src/app/Shell.tsx.

requirements.title: Backup and restore include productivity collections
requirements.statement: A full backup with includeSensitive true must carry time_entries, automation_rules, productivity_receipts, task props, and the DEPENDS_ON, SERVES_GOAL, WAITING_ON, and FOR edges. Share-safe export continues to drop receipts and anything tied to sensitive records. Restore must round-trip those collections on an isolated database.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-09-11 from the Task 10 plan. Enforced by apps/api/src/services/export.ts and documented in docs/runbooks/restore-drill.md.

requirements.title: Private compute-on-read analytics
requirements.statement: Productivity analytics are computed on read from records plus revisions, declare history completeness, exclude sensitive records by default, and send no telemetry. Silence is not a zero.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-09-11 from ADR 0012. Enforced by apps/api/src/services/productivity/analytics.ts and asserted by docs/PRIVACY.md.

requirements.title: Provenance is visible on the record
requirements.statement: Every record surface must be able to show where a fact came from (source, source reference, and confidence) as inspectable provenance rather than hidden columns, and provenance must be filterable wherever records are searched.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007, and corrected the same day: the first note claimed the surfaces did not present provenance, which undersold shipped reality: the source-and-confidence chip was already a design-system primitive on eight screens. What was genuinely missing, the source reference, now renders on the record header beside the chip, and the search grammar filters on source. The chip predates this identifier; the reference cites it in apps/web/src/routes/Record.tsx.

requirements.title: The ledger answers what changed
requirements.statement: A ledger must answer what changed since the operator last looked: a reverse-chronological feed over the revision history, each entry naming the operation and linking to its record and its diff.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007 and shipped the same day: apps/api/src/routes/v1/ledger.ts reads the feed, apps/web/src/routes/Ledger.tsx presents it under the Today hub, and entries label themselves from their stored snapshots so deleted records keep their names. The revision substrate predates the surface by design.

requirements.title: History opens into field-level diffs
requirements.statement: A record's history must open into field-level diffs between revisions (what changed, from what, to what), not only a count of revision ticks.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007 and shipped the same day: the record screen's history rows disclose the stored field diff: a row with changes unfolds, a row without stays a row. The diffs were in the revision rows all along.

requirements.title: An atom cites its provenance
requirements.statement: A resume atom must be able to cite the records that evidence it. Provenance is held for review and is never rendered into the compiled document.

requirements.title: Job descriptions parse to weighted keywords
requirements.statement: Pasting a job description must produce a set of weighted keywords deterministically, with no call to an external model.

requirements.title: The parsed keyword set is editable
requirements.statement: The parsed keyword set must be fully editable downstream of the parser: keywords can be added, removed, and reweighted.

requirements.title: Atom scoring decomposes exactly
requirements.statement: Every atom must be scored against the active target as soon as one exists, independently of selection, and the per-keyword contributions shown in the breakdown must sum to the reported relevance exactly.

requirements.title: Deterministic selection to a page budget
requirements.statement: Selection must fill the page budget deterministically, so that identical inputs give identical proposals. Pinned atoms are forced in, a per-role bullet partition constraint applies, and a manual mode lets the operator hand-pick and order the selection instead.

requirements.title: Template line model and page-fill meter
requirements.statement: Each template must carry a line model that estimates how many rendered lines a block of content will occupy, driving a page-fill meter against the one-page budget. The estimate must stay within a stated tolerance of real compiled output, verified by compiling calibration fixtures.

requirements.reconstruction_note: Asserted only by the range citation FR-RES-001..018 on the resume-engine row of docs/ROADMAP.md, which lists eleven features across eighteen identifiers. Positional mapping would be invention, so no statement is recorded.

requirements.title: Build the resume model and render LaTeX
requirements.statement: Finalizing must assemble the selected evidence into a resume model, render it through the chosen template to LaTeX, and submit it for compilation.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Recovered by elimination: the identifier appears only inside a grouped citation, and every other identifier in that group is pinned individually elsewhere, leaving exactly one unattributed behavior in the group text. Here the group is FR-RES-011/012/013 in apps/api/src/routes/v1/resumes.ts, whose text reads "Build the resume model, render LaTeX, and compile"; FR-RES-012 is pinned as LaTeX escaping and FR-RES-013 as compile-service degradation.

requirements.title: User content is escaped before it reaches LaTeX
requirements.statement: All operator content must be escaped and sanitized before it is written into LaTeX, neutralizing shell-escape and injection attempts. This requirement is security-critical and is verified by property-based fuzzing that the escaped output always compiles.

requirements.title: Compilation degrades rather than fails the flow
requirements.statement: Requests to the compile service must be authenticated by a message authentication code, and an unavailable compile service must degrade the affected step rather than fail the whole flow.

requirements.title: One-page fit loop after compile
requirements.statement: When a compiled document overflows one page, a bounded fit loop must plan and apply reduction steps until it fits or the step cap is reached.

requirements.title: Coverage gate on the compiled document
requirements.statement: Finalizing must extract the text of the compiled PDF and verify that it covers at least ninety-five percent of the selected evidence before the document is accepted.

requirements.reconstruction_note: Asserted only by the range citation FR-RES-001..018 on the resume-engine row of docs/ROADMAP.md, which lists eleven features across eighteen identifiers. Positional mapping would be invention, so no statement is recorded.

Asserted only by the range citation FR-RES-001..018 on the resume-engine row of docs/ROADMAP.md, which lists eleven features across eighteen identifiers. Positional mapping would be invention, so no statement is recorded.

requirements.title: Marking a resume sent creates the application record
requirements.statement: Marking a resume as sent must create or link an application node, so that the career pipeline is a consequence of the send rather than a separate manual step.

requirements.title: Saved outputs can be recompiled and re-uploaded
requirements.statement: A saved resume output must be recompilable, re-uploading its PDF and LaTeX source, so that a lost or corrupted artifact can be recovered.

requirements.title: Cover letters are stored as structured drafts
requirements.statement: A cover letter must be storable against a target as structured blocks of hook, body, and closer, each sourced from text or from an atom, with full create, read, update, and delete support.
requirements.reconstruction_note: The model, the generation interface and now the compile pair are all shipped. The deferral this note used to record closed with FR-RES-021: a letter stores its recipient, salutation and closing, and finalize keeps the PDF and the source as its artifacts.

requirements.title: Letters compile like résumés
requirements.statement: A finalized cover letter must compile to the same artifact pair as a résumé (PDF plus source) through the same sandboxed compiler, with the same escape guarantees and the same graceful degradation when the compiler is unreachable.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007; delivered 2026-08-27. The blocker was upstream of the letter: the build service calibrated every template in templates/ at Docker image build and hard-failed anything that was not a one-page résumé, so the first letter template would have failed the image build before it could be used. Calibration is now per template, declared in each directory's calibration.json, and a directory without one fails loudly rather than being skipped. On top of that, templates/letter-classic, a renderer that goes through the same LaTeX escape path résumés use rather than a second one, and compile, finalize and artifact routes that mirror the résumé pair, including answering 200 with the source and leaving the letter in draft when the compiler is unreachable.

requirements.title: Authenticated and allow-listed access
requirements.statement: Every request must be authenticated against a verified identity and authorized against the configured owner, denying by default. The development sign-in shortcut is available only behind an explicit flag.

requirements.title: Algorithm constants are editable, validated, versioned settings
requirements.statement: The tunable constants of the intelligence layer must live in one place and be exposed through a constants editor with validated ranges, versioning, and live preview. Every algorithm reads its constants from that place, so a settings override is a single object spread over the documented defaults. Nothing in the layer is learned.
requirements.reconstruction_note: The phrase "constants editor, validated ranges, versioned, live preview" is quoted directly from the original requirement text inside packages/core/src/algorithms/constants.ts, which preserves it verbatim.

requirements.title: Health page
requirements.statement: A status route must report the health of the database, storage, and build service, together with live record counts.

requirements.title: Sensitive records are opt-in for export
requirements.statement: Records marked sensitive must be excluded from an export unless the operator explicitly opts in.

requirements.title: Unified ranked full-text search
requirements.statement: Search must run a single ranked full-text query over record titles, subtitles, notes, and properties, built from live data and scoped to the active data space.

requirements.title: Composable filter grammar
requirements.statement: Search must accept a composable filter query that parses into a clause tree applied on top of the text query, and the parsed clauses must be reflected back to the operator as visible chips.

requirements.title: Deterministic ranking
requirements.statement: Search ranking must be deterministic, combining exact-title bonus, recency, and pinned status.

requirements.title: Fuzzy quick-switcher
requirements.statement: A command palette must offer a fuzzy match over record titles alongside actions, in one list with two lanes.

requirements.title: Imports can propose field-level updates
requirements.statement: A staged import that matches an existing record by identity key must be able to propose field-level updates, presented as a per-field diff for review; nothing updates without acceptance, and a rejected proposal leaves the record untouched.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 under ADR 0007; delivered 2026-08-27. The blocker was upstream of the proposal: the identity-key machinery and its GIN index had been in the repository the whole time and no non-bundle importer ever populated a key, so nothing could match on a second run and every staged row could only ever be new. vCard, iCal, LinkedIn and bookmarks now synthesize a key from what the source genuinely identifies a row by, and a row carrying nothing identifying stays a create rather than being matched on a hash of its display name. A matched row becomes a proposal carrying a per-field diff; nothing is written without acceptance and rejecting one leaves the record byte-identical.

requirements.title: Re-import is longitudinal
requirements.statement: Re-importing from the same source must be longitudinal: unchanged rows converge silently on their identity keys, changed rows become update proposals, and the batch report counts created, updated, unchanged, and skipped separately.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 under ADR 0007; delivered 2026-08-27. The batch report counts created, updated, unchanged and skipped apart, which needed the sync bookkeeping fields excluded from the comparison first: last_synced_at moves on every run, so a byte-identical row looked changed and the unchanged bucket would have read zero forever while appearing to satisfy this requirement. Rollback is per node and rev-guarded, so a record edited since the import is reported as skipped with the reason and the rest of the batch still rolls back.

requirements.title: Life map
requirements.statement: The graph must be explorable as a navigable life map with a keyboard and list equivalent and URL-backed state.

requirements.title: Chronograph timeline
requirements.statement: Career and life records must be explorable on a timeline with a keyboard and list equivalent and URL-backed state.

requirements.title: Atlas of places
requirements.statement: Places in the graph must be explorable on a navigable map with a keyboard and list equivalent and URL-backed state.

requirements.title: The Today aggregate is one call
requirements.statement: The dashboard must assemble its widgets from a single aggregate request rather than one request per widget.

requirements.title: Timeline brush feeds a review surface
requirements.statement: Selecting a range on the timeline must carry that range into a review surface for the records it covers.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Recovered by elimination: the identifier appears only inside a grouped citation, and every other identifier in that group is pinned individually elsewhere, leaving exactly one unattributed behavior in the group text. Here the group is FR-VIS-002/005 in apps/web/src/features/timeline/TimelineView.tsx, whose text reads "Chronograph, career/life timeline with brush to review"; FR-VIS-002 is pinned as the chronograph itself by the Explore row of docs/ROADMAP.md, leaving the brush-to-review behavior.

requirements.title: Keyboard focus is always visible
requirements.statement: Every element that can receive keyboard focus must show a focus indicator that meets WCAG 2.1 AA, and the indicator must survive a forced-colors display mode. The indicator is defined once for the whole product rather than per component, so a new control cannot ship without one.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Recovered from packages/ui/src/styles/base.css:123, its only citation in the repository, which reads "Visible focus everywhere (WCAG 2.1 AA: NFR-A11Y-001)" above a bare :focus-visible rule that replaces the user-agent outline with var(--ae-focus-ring), defined at packages/ui/src/styles/tokens.css:131 as a two-pixel background halo and a two-pixel accent ring. The word "everywhere" and the unqualified selector are the evidence for the scope; the @media (forced-colors: active) block at base.css:151, which restores an outline because a box-shadow is discarded in that mode, is the evidence that the indicator was required to survive rather than merely to exist. Like NFR-MNT-002, this identifier was missed by an earlier pass of this register, but for a different reason: the citation reader's family pattern could not spell A11Y, so the citation was unreadable rather than unread. See the FAMILY constant in scripts/docs/lib/citations.mjs.

requirements.title: Every routed screen is scanned for accessibility
requirements.statement: Every route the application mounts must be scanned by an automated accessibility check in the end-to-end suite, and the count of scanned screens is a ratchet: it may grow and must not silently shrink. Visual surfaces (the graph, the timeline, the map) must each keep a keyboard-operable list equivalent, and motion must respect the reduced-motion preference.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007, not recovered from a citation. Enforced by the end-to-end ratchets in docs/testing/e2e-ratchets.json, which check accessibility coverage by screen, and by the list equivalents the explore surfaces ship; the enforcing files do not cite this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: Leaving is a supported feature
requirements.statement: The complete graph must export to open formats (JSON Lines per collection and a Markdown vault readable by plain-text tools) with a checksummed manifest, and a restore from that bundle must round-trip document identity. No commercial state may degrade export: a locked workspace keeps its way out.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. The behavior is enforced by apps/api/src/services/export.ts and services/restore.ts, and the locked-workspace escape hatch by the entitlement gate in apps/api/src/middleware/workspace.ts; none of them cites this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here. FR-001, FR-EXP-010 and FR-SET-007 state the functional halves; this entry states the portability promise they add up to.

requirements.title: Compiled documents are reproducible and parseable
requirements.statement: Compiling the same document twice with a pinned source date must produce byte-identical artifacts, so an operator can prove that an archived file is the one they sent. Compiled output must stay parseable by applicant tracking systems: one page, standard fonts, no content that only a human renderer can read.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. Enforced by SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH handling in services/buildsvc and the template contract's strict mode; the enforcing code does not cite this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: The module boundary is enforced rather than agreed
requirements.statement: No workspace outside packages/core may import another workspace's internal modules. The boundary must be machine-enforced so that a violation fails the build rather than depending on review to notice it.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Recovered from the header of eslint.config.js, which names this identifier beside INT-2 and states the rule the configuration enforces. This identifier was missed by the first pass of this register, which read only the source trees; a root-level configuration file carried the sole citation. It was recovered by docs/generated/traceability.json, which reads every tracked file, and it is the reason that generator scans the whole repository rather than a chosen subset.

requirements.title: Undocumented surfaces fail the build
requirements.statement: A route, package, algorithm, runbook, or template added without prose documentation must fail continuous integration: prose coverage is a ratchet whose undocumented list may only shrink. A source module without a colocated test fails the coverage map the same way. Documentation and tests are not favors to the future; they are the price of merging.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. Enforced by scripts/check-docs-coverage.mjs and scripts/check-test-coverage-map.mjs; neither cites this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: Stated and rehearsed recovery objectives
requirements.statement: A production or hosted deployment must state its recovery point and recovery time objectives, take scheduled encrypted backups to storage off the application host, and demonstrate the stated objectives by a rehearsed restore drill on a recorded cadence.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. The mechanics exist (scripts/backup-to-s3.sh, docs/runbooks/restore-drill.md, FR-EXP-012 and FR-EXP-013), but the objectives themselves are numbers this repository cannot supply: backup retention and recovery targets are among the operational facts docs/CLOUD-LAUNCH.md records as needing outside confirmation. The stated remainder is exactly those numbers and their cadence.

requirements.title: A lapsed workspace stays readable, exportable, and honest
requirements.statement: When payment lapses, a hosted workspace becomes read-only rather than deleted: reads, export, billing, and sign-out keep working while every other mutation is refused by the server with the access state and the way out named in the refusal. The interface must present the lock at the controls it disables, not only announce it globally.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. The server half is enforced by the method-based entitlement gate in apps/api/src/middleware/workspace.ts; the shell banner names the lock, and the shared write entry points (the new-record menu, both capture triggers, the entity form dialog, and the bulk bars) disable themselves with the lock explained at the control. The stated remainder is the long tail of per-screen inline mutations (the interaction logger, tailoring autosave, reminder completion), which still rely on the server refusal being surfaced rather than pre-empted.

requirements.title: The web bundle is budgeted
requirements.statement: The production web bundle must stay inside enforced size budgets, heavy visualization libraries must load only on the routes that use them, and a build carrying development artifacts must be refused before its size is even measured.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. Enforced by scripts/check-web-budgets.mjs against docs/testing/web-budgets.json and by route-level lazy loading in apps/web/src/App.tsx; the enforcing files do not cite this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: The interactive envelope is fifty thousand nodes
requirements.statement: Interactive surfaces must stay responsive against a graph of about fifty thousand nodes and two hundred and fifty thousand edges. Inside that envelope, the whole graph is read at most once per request, per-type counts come from grouped queries, and a rendered view that caps its elements must say that it capped rather than degrade silently.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007, naming the design envelope the code already assumes: FR-102 and FR-104 state the read rules, and the explore services cap their elements. The envelope number itself appears in no source file; recording it here is what makes exceeding it a requirements change rather than a surprise.

requirements.title: No runtime AI, as a numbered requirement
requirements.statement: The product must make no runtime call to an external AI provider and must carry no AI-provider client in any dependency manifest. Every intelligent behavior is a deterministic function whose inputs and factors the operator can inspect. This is the boundary ADR 0003 chose; it is restated as a numbered requirement so that changing it is a requirements change, not a drift.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. Verifiable by inspection of every dependency manifest under apps/, packages/, and services/, and asserted in prose by README.md, PRODUCT.md, and docs/adr/0003-deterministic-intelligence.md; no code cites the identifier because the requirement is the absence of code.

requirements.title: No telemetry
requirements.statement: The product must collect no behavioural analytics, embed no tracking or telemetry client, and send no operator content to any service the operator did not configure. What an operator does with their own record is not data for anyone else.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. Verifiable by the absence of any analytics dependency in the manifests and asserted by docs/PRIVACY.md; the error boundary in apps/web/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx states in prose that no telemetry pipeline exists to report to.

requirements.title: Every ranking explains itself
requirements.statement: Any ranked or derived number shown to the operator must decompose into named factors the interface presents, and where a sum is claimed the parts must sum exactly. A recommendation that cannot show its arithmetic must not ship.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007, generalizing what FR-CON-006 and FR-RES-007 each state for one surface into the rule every future surface is held to. Enforced today by the factor-chip decompositions across the ask, intros, tailor, and dashboard surfaces.

requirements.title: Productivity performance budgets fail closed
requirements.statement: A 10,000-task performance workspace must stay inside documented budgets for matrix interaction, analytics latency, route chunks, memory, and API query counts on GET /tasks and GET /analytics?window=30. A check that cannot measure a budget must fail rather than only log, unless the environment blocker is recorded and the gate is not claimed passed.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-09-11 from the Task 10 plan. Enforced by scripts/check-productivity-budgets.mjs against docs/testing/productivity-budgets.json.

requirements.title: Multi-document writes are atomic
requirements.statement: Multi-document writes must go through the transaction boundary so that imports, merges, and resume finalize are atomic. Every mutation is append-only audited, writing the record together with a revision row carrying the full snapshot, the field diff, the operation, and the source. Deletes are soft, and edges to a deleted node are hidden by query filters rather than removed, so that restore is lossless.

requirements.title: No mutation fails silently
requirements.statement: Every failed mutation must surface to the operator: a global handler guarantees an error report whenever no local handler takes responsibility, and loading, empty, over-filtered, and failed must be four distinct presentations on every surface. A failed load must never render as an empty list.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. Enforced by the mutation-cache error net in apps/web/src/main.tsx and by the feedback grammar the end-to-end suite asserts screen by screen. The four-state distinction is its most-tested invariant; the enforcing code does not cite this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: The identity boundary is default-deny
requirements.statement: Every request is denied unless it carries a verified identity that authorization admits: the configured owner on a self-hosted install, a server-resolved workspace membership when the hosted plane is enabled. Authorization failures are neutral and never reveal the allow-list. The development sign-in shortcut answers loopback requests only and is off in production.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007, modelling the trust boundary the T1 marker sits on; cited beside that marker in the header of apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts. FR-015 and FR-SET-001 state the functional behaviors; this entry states the boundary they defend.

requirements.title: The storage boundary is a single adapter
requirements.statement: Object storage is reached only through one adapter interface: uploads are content-addressed, delivery uses short-lived signed URLs, and no public object URL is ever handed out. Swapping the provider is a change to one binding, not a search across the application.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007, modelling the trust boundary the T5 marker sits on; cited beside that marker in the header of apps/api/src/services/storage/adapter.ts. INT-5 and FR-CAP-004 state the interface and the dedup rule; this entry states the boundary posture.

requirements.title: The compiler is sandboxed and authenticated
requirements.statement: Document compilation accepts only requests signed with a shared-secret message authentication code, runs untrusted input in an isolated container with no network egress, works in a per-request scratch directory, and ships no published fallback key. Operator content is escaped before it reaches the compiler.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. Enforced by services/buildsvc/src/server.ts together with FR-027, FR-RES-012, and FR-RES-013, which state three of its clauses individually; the isolation posture as a whole had no identifier until this one.

requirements.title: Secrets stay out of records and history
requirements.statement: Credentials live in the environment or a protected secret store, never in application records, exports, or version control. A surface reports a credential's presence, never its value. A stored third-party token is encrypted at rest and is never returned to the browser.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Authored 2026-08-26 as a product decision under ADR 0007. FR-004 states the storage rule and the presence-not-value rule for one surface; apps/api/src/services/secrets.ts enforces the store and the GitHub token path enforces encryption at rest. The enforcing code does not cite this identifier, so the attribution is recorded here.

requirements.title: Google identity provider integration
requirements.statement: Vitae authenticates a person against Google through the Firebase Web SDK in the browser and verifies the resulting identity token on the server before any request is served. A development sign-in shortcut may stand in for the provider only when it is explicitly enabled by configuration.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Recovered from three independent citations that each name the identifier and describe one face of the same integration: packages/config/src/env.ts:36 marks the authentication configuration block, apps/web/src/lib/firebase.ts:2 the browser sign-in bootstrap, and apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:2 server-side verification. docs/ROADMAP.md:13 pairs the identifier with the same behavior.

requirements.title: Vitae is a module that owns its data plane
requirements.statement: Vitae owns its storage and exposes it only through its own interfaces. No other workspace reaches into Vitae's internals, and Vitae reaches into no other workspace's internals.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Recovered from two citations that agree: eslint.config.js:2 states the rule as enforced, and docs/specs/merge-plan.md:3 states it as architectural intent. The statement recorded here is what both assert; neither is extended by the other.

requirements.title: One authoritative palette for the whole interface
requirements.statement: Every colour, dimension and type decision in the interface resolves to a single declared token set. No screen defines its own palette, so a change to the identity is a change in one file rather than a search across the app.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Recovered from packages/ui/src/styles/tokens.css:2, which names the identifier and calls the file the single authoritative palette. The same header records the 2026-08 Quiet identity and its standing bans, which scripts/check-brand-bans.mjs enforces.

requirements.title: Attachment storage is reached only through an adapter
requirements.statement: The application talks to object storage through one interface, so the provider can be replaced by changing a single binding. Uploads are content-addressed so identical bytes are stored once, and delivery is private through short-lived signed URLs rather than public object URLs.
requirements.reconstruction_note: Recovered from apps/api/src/services/storage/adapter.ts:2, which names the identifier and states the swap requirement, the content-addressing rule and the private-delivery rule in the same header. The dedup clause there cites FR-CAP-004 separately, so it is attributed to that identifier and only summarized here.

docs/specs/merge-plan.md:3 is the only citation, and it names INT-6 jointly with INT-2 in a single sentence about owning a data plane. INT-2 is independently pinned by eslint.config.js, but elimination does not apply to a two-member group whose members may state different halves of one sentence: splitting it would invent the division rather than recover it.
